text:
riley: quick thread — want to run a compact battlecard + landing experiment next week to see which message actually drives higher-quality infra/platform leads. short window, small budget.

juan: what are the candidate frames?

riley: three distinct hooks: 1) "Pay-per-inference transparency" (clear cost breakdowns + reserved options), 2) "Predictable latency, even at scale" (fallbacks + reserved pools), 3) "One SDK, every environment" (no rework for private/dedicated).

faye: solid. lets make the language pragmatic: no big % claims. use phrasing like "real-world unit-cost reductions" and "consistent p95 latency" with a tiny benchmark tile.

rebecca: for CTAs let's test two funnels: "Launch sandbox" (immediate PLG access) and "Request solutions call" (enterprise). different routing should reveal intent.

design-bot: creative asks noted: 2 headline treatments per hook, 3 hero comps, small hero that hints infra (diagram) vs hero that hints ops (monitoring UI).

juan: routing plan (examples): /launch-sandbox?utm=hookA and /request-call?utm=hookA. capture `lead_intent` dropdown (exploring-hosted|evaluating-dedicated|privacy-first).

ops-bot: task created: MKG-2145. Routes: /launch-sandbox?utm=hookA and /request-call?utm=hookA and equivalents for hookB/hookC. Staging previews at https://staging.redwood.test/mkg/2145

faye: benchmark tile: keep it descriptive not precise. example copy: "Internal test: typical p95 latency 80-250ms depending on model/seq; batching + KV cache reduced per-token compute in production runs." label as "internal examples; results vary."

riley: good. also include one-line model-quality note: "Model outputs align with open weights; our focus is serving economics & stability." short and neutral.

rebecca: SDR playbook: short rebut lines per hook and procurement quick answers. e.g., cost -> "We surface per-route spend and reserved options in Console; many customers improve unit economics without changing models." latency -> "Fallback orchestration + SLA pools keep tail latency predictable." portability -> "Same SDK and API surface reduces migration work." keep all <2 sentences.

juan: add a procurement template to the battlecard with checklist items: SLAs, data residency, audit logs, pricing model, rollout timeline. helps SDRs close faster.

ads-bot: paid test recommended: LinkedIn carousel (hookA vs hookB) + small X/Twitter test for product-first. budget: $900. run Thu-Mon.

riley: timeline: headlines + hero comps Tue EOD, landing variants up Wed AM, ads Thu. collect CTR -> qualified conversion and lead_intent distribution.

faye: analytics: capture `utm`, `lead_intent`, and a tiny hidden field `creative_variant`. dashboards to show which hook yields more enterprise-form submissions.

rebecca: CTA microcopy variants: "Launch sandbox (instant)" vs "Request a 15-min solutions call" — test which reduces friction for enterprise.

design-bot: will upload comps by Tue 3pm and provide alt colorways for each hero.

juan: will write three compact headline families and two rebut lines per competitor claim (cloud managed endpoints; pure infra vendors; AI API providers). keep rebut lines direct and non-technical-friendly.

riley: legal note: avoid absolute guarantees, mark benchmarks as examples, and tag any percentage claims with source. i'll loop legal for a quick review.

ops-bot: reminder scheduled: MKG-2145 deploy check Wed 09:10 UTC.

rebecca: final deliverables recap: battlecard snippet + procurement checklist, 6 headline variants, 3 hero comps, two landing flows with UTMs, SDR rebut lines, benchmark tile, ads creative. i'll coordinate SDR training Wed afternoon.

riley: perfect. will post the draft battlecard in #marketing for fast feedback Wed. thanks everyone! :rocket:
